text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma

name: Opus
text: Last game you spent day 2 on me while Sonnet and Haiku sat quiet. Watch who pushes early this time, not who talks loudest.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: I'll play the hero and let Haiku take the heat if we have to push someone.

name: Gemma

name: Haiku
text: Terra's "listening fresh" line sounded like a dodge to me, honestly. Who's with me?
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

Night falls on Palermo. The killers strike, but the doctor got there first. A new day dawns in Palermo, and nobody is out.

The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the killer, Gemma the killer, Sol the officer, Luna the doctor, Terra the citizen, Opus the citizen.
Haiku's card said killer, and the town got its man.

name: Opus
text: Proud that I pushed Gemma on day one instead of Sol. I regret hammering Sonnet after Haiku was already the obvious card; that read was mine, and it was wrong.

Sol claimed to be the officer on Day 1 and said he had been shown Gemma as a killer. The town voted Gemma out that day, and her card showed killer, which backed up Sol's claim. On Day 2, Haiku spent his time pushing Sonnet's early vote, and his own vote against Sol, made alongside Gemma, never got a clear explanation. The town voted Haiku out that day, and his card showed killer, so the town won. Sonnet, Opus and Haiku each admitted a mistake after the game.
